We further illustrate the utilization of CDT to analyze and support decision-making to enhance the case study system according to its objectives. • Multi-flow Process Mining (MFPM) automatically extracts Multidimensional Stochastic Petri Nets (MDSPNs). • MDSPNs can serve as core simulation models for Comprehensive Digital Twins (CDTs) of manufacturing systems. • MDSPNs capture systems’ behavior in different dimensions, such as time, energy, and waste, in a coherent model. • CDTs enable data-driven simulation and multi-objective decision support in manufacturing systems. • A hot forging case study demonstrates efficiency and sustainability gains using CDTs. • MDPySPN enables CDT simulation and supports multi-objective optimization and decision support.

title: An improved large language model and knowledge graph integration method for automated machining process base construction
abstract: The Machining Process Knowledge Base (MPKB) is foundational to intelligent process decision-making, directly impacting manufacturing efficiency and quality. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in automated MPKB construction, they face a critical challenge in manufacturing: industrial knowledge graph (KG) schemas often exceed the context windows of lightweight LLMs deployable by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This limitation forces the construction process to operate with incomplete schema information, leading to missed entity relationships, semantic heterogeneity, and conceptual ambiguities in the MPKB. This study proposes an improved LLM-KG collaborative framework that overcomes these limitations through: (1) employing a staged, schema-decoupled extraction strategy, which enables open triple collection without injecting the full schema; (2) introducing a Code-Style knowledge representation method that efficiently encodes complex machining schemas, reducing the semantic load while maintaining structural integrity; and (3) constructing a retrieval-driven pipeline for semantic standardization that integrates dynamic schema segmentation and bidirectional validation, utilizing LLMs to achieve interpretable synonym merging and eliminate heterogeneity. This study empirically validated the proposed approach using machining process data provided by an aviation enterprise. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves at least a 3.3% improvement in MPKB construction quality and a 25% increase in machining process quality metrics compared to the other baseline models. The implementation and data have been made available on GitHub to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

title: A comprehensive framework for computationally efficient system-level design optimization of machine tools
abstract: Mass reduction of machine tool components is a crucial task that can improve performance, accuracy, and energy efficiency. System-level optimization, where multiple components are simultaneously optimized, is noted in the literature as a challenging necessity for complete performance improvement of machine tools. Existing methods focus on optimizing the machine tool components individually, neglecting the critical effects of simultaneous modification on the machine performance and thorough exploration of the design space. To the authors’ knowledge, for the first time in the literature, this paper presents a comprehensive framework for system-level machine tool design optimization considering the most significant multi-objective performance indicators for the machining process. Static and dynamic stiffness, thermal and dynamic stability, and fatigue life are evaluated as performance indicators using a multi-objective finite element response set that includes coupled thermal-structural, modal, and frequency response analyses. A minimal parameter set approach is proposed which uses the linear guide joints to minimize the number of design variables, addressing the challenge of increased computational cost in system-level modeling. Machine responses during optimization iterations are predicted by a machine learning model trained on the machine tool’s multi-objective finite element response set, achieving higher accuracy than commonly used polynomial-based methods. A constraint relaxation method is proposed that permits limited degradation relative to the base design, yielding designs that substantially outperform those obtained from unconstrained optimization while avoiding over-constraining. Up to 20 % mass reduction is achieved across the machine tool components while the performance indicators are either improved or maintained with negligible degradation.

title: Heterogeneous multi-agent fleet control system for material handling in a Software-Defined Factory
abstract: The conventional Industry 4.0 architecture of manufacturing and warehousing is hardware-centric, limiting flexibility and adaptability. The material handling systems deploy heterogeneous multiple agents that have an application or environment-specific discrete control layer. This work presents the concept of a Software-Defined Factory and its control system for a software-centric control. The software-defined factory integrates industrial hardware and software systems, hosting the control system, AI, simulation, and digital twins to enable seamless material flow throughout the factory through heterogeneous multi-agent control. The presented control system has a centralized architecture designed with a bottom-up approach for commercial systems. It manages communication, localization, navigation, and task allocation in a heterogeneous multi-vendor fleet deployed in real-world scenarios. The latency, accuracy, repeatability, planning-level scalability, and path execution evaluations of the proposed system were conducted with heterogeneous fleets. The operation of overhead hoist transport vehicles with automated guided vehicles on a scaled semiconductor manufacturing shop floor demonstrated heterogeneous hardware integration for material handling in industrial settings. The proposed system has potential to mitigate major challenges in deployment, data interoperability, and hardware dependency for diverse industrial applications, including manufacturing, warehousing, and inspection.

title: From insight to action: Embodied multi-agent system integrating vision language model for digital twin-assisted human-robot collaborative assembly
abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly has emerged as a core pivotal technology for the high-efficiency manufacturing of complex products. Nevertheless, existing systems still face critical challenges: the difficulty in translating unstructured user assembly intent into standardized task execution, insufficient scenario-specific perceptual understanding of assembly contexts, and the lack of robust safety guarantees and intuitive operational guidance. To address these critical challenges, a novel embodied multi-agent system (MAS) integrated with a vision-language model (VLM) for digital twin (DT)-enabled HRC assembly is proposed in this paper, which constructs a closed-loop workflow encompassing multi-modal perception and reasoning (“insight”) as well as autonomous robot execution and collaboration (“action”). First, a collaborative embodied multi-agent framework is constructed to encompass task management, perception, reasoning, robot execution, and augmented reality (AR) execution, enabling seamless transition from unstructured assembly intent to standardized HRC implementation. Second, domain knowledge fine-tuning is performed on the VLM to achieve end-to-end understanding of visual inputs and semantic alignment with textual descriptions in assembly scenarios, thereby providing precise scenario-adapted perceptual support. Third, a cyber-physical mapping environment is built using DT technology to facilitate simulation verification of robot motion planning and real-time scene mapping for AR-guided operations. The experimental results verify that the proposed system effectively mitigates the limitations of existing HRC assembly systems, enabling efficient, adaptive, and safe collaborative assembly while laying a solid foundation for the intelligent upgrading of complex product assembly processes.

title: A Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph retrieval-augmented generation framework for intelligent maintenance
abstract: As industrial equipment is increasingly applied in manufacturing, it is necessary to adopt advanced maintenance techniques to ensure stable equipment operation. Maintenance decision support is essential for industrial equipment, but information fragmentation and complex reasoning hinder its progress. To address these challenges, we propose MAKG (Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph), a framework that synergizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a multi-agent system for intelligent industrial equipment maintenance. The MAKG framework uses these Large Language Models (LLM) agents to work together, drawing information from a diverse knowledge base to produce coordinated responses to equipment faults. Our method focuses on fine-tuning the embedding models with domain-specific data. This approach avoids the high computational cost of re-training the entire LLM and improves performance in the specific industrial context. In the experimental study, the MAKG framework was validated using real-world industrial operation and maintenance data, achieving a reasoning accuracy of 90.1% and demonstrating its potential for intelligent maintenance of industrial equipment. Code is available at https://github.com/LAM2360/MAKG_demo/tree/master.

title: CMDF-LSTM-driven feature point identification of CNC G code leveraging geometric and kinematic information
abstract: Identifying feature points in G code is crucial for improving machining accuracy and efficiency in CNC machining. Traditional methods rely on engineers’ experience and predefined geometric thresholds, which commonly fail to account for the actual kinematic and kinetic conditions of the machine tool. This paper proposes a novel, data-driven approach to feature point identification by leveraging both kinematic and geometric information from G code trajectories. A five-phase jerk-limited S-shape interpolation algorithm is employed to generate kinematic characteristics for each point along the trajectory, while three key geometric features are defined to support accurate identification. Building on this, we propose a CNC Machining Data Flow-based Long Short-Term Memory (CMDF-LSTM) model that combines both kinematic and geometric data to automate feature point identification. A training dataset consisting of 12 workpieces and over 105 G code files is generated using Mastercam, with more than 107 setpoints computed through interpolation. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and the real-time feed rate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system further demonstrate the effectiveness. The cutting experiments are conducted to verify that the machining defects occur at the feature points identified by our method, and quantitative surface roughness measurements at the machined surface further enhance the credibility of experimental conclusions. In addition, the real-time feedrate recorded during machining process and cutting forces monitored by intelligent spindle system demonstrate the effectiveness from multiple dimensions. This approach provides a scalable and efficient solution for feature point identification in real-world CNC machining applications.

title: Leveraging large language models for smart manufacturing: Reviews, enablers, challenges, and opportunities
abstract: Smart manufacturing is transforming manufacturing landscapes through the integration of advanced information and communication technologies. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized artificial intelligence (AI). However, the application of LLMs in smart manufacturing remains underexplored to address the domain-specific challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and analysis of LLM-enabled smart manufacturing. The latest advancements in LLM for smart manufacturing and the key techniques in LLMs are first reviewed. Subsequently, the key enablers for deploying LLM for smart manufacturing are explored, which include the knowledge graph (KG), agent system, and model context protocol (MCP). Then, the capability across four critical manufacturing domains, including product design, process optimization, predictive maintenance, and remanufacturing are systematically analyzed. Finally, the challenges and opportunities of scaling laws, data privacy and security concerns, the interpretability of LLMs, and the domain-specific knowledge integration within the manufacturing context are also discussed. The outcomes of this research contribute to a responsible and efficient adoption of LLMs, laying a foundation for advancing smart manufacturing practices.

title: Neural–symbolic reasoning for end-of-life product identification in robot-assisted disassembly
abstract: Efficient recycling and reuse of end-of-life products through robot-assisted disassembly has attracted widespread attention in sustainable manufacturing industry. In the robot-assisted disassembly system, the high-precision identification of products and their components is the premise of autonomous disassembly. A series of product identification methods based on deep learning in literature can well identify specific categories of components such as screws. However, different service conditions make products in industrial scenarios highly uncertain in terms of component status, shape and position changes, which make it impossible to predefine categories for products and components, and to obtain high-quality training data sets for new categories in advance. These obstacles make the application of the identification methods to industrial scenarios still challenging. In this paper, a two-stage product identification method based on neural–symbolic reasoning is proposed. In the first stage, deep learning-based methods are used to detect component primitives with limited categories, rather than directly detecting components whose categories cannot be predefined. In the second stage, the logic rules embedded in the word vector space are used to program the detected primitives to infer the semantics of the component to be detected. In addition, a primitive sampling method is proposed to generate new rules by sampling existing rules in the word vector space to improve the generalization of the proposed identification method. The results show a significant increase from 20.01% to 80.89% in successful component identification for the PC product family, along with considerable improvement for others. Code and data are available at http://github.com/nowheresin/neural-symbolic-reasoning-product-identification/.

title: LLM-driven discrete-event simulation: A generative AI framework for automated model generation, adaptation, and evaluation in manufacturing
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) framework for automating the generation, adaptation, and evaluation of discrete-event simulation (DES) models in manufacturing. The approach integrates multiple large language models (LLMs) with a structured blueprint model and targeted human-in-the-loop controls to create executable simulation models from heterogeneous production data, implement targeted modifications, and interpret simulation outcomes. The workflow incorporates prompt engineering, zero- and one-shot implementations, and evaluator–optimizer loops. 21 experimental runs on two industrial case studies from a Swedish automotive manufacturer demonstrate that LLMs can support DES model generation and scenario exploration through a hybrid approach combining automation with human oversight. The results underline both the potential and current limitations of LLM-driven simulation, particularly regarding output consistency and generalizability. Future research should extend the method to more complex manufacturing systems and investigate the role of emerging autonomous Gen-AI tools in simulation-based decision support. • LLM-driven workflow automating discrete-event simulation (DES) model generation, adaptation, and evaluation. • Integrates multiple LLMs with a structured blueprint model and human-in-the-loop oversight. • Systematically tested across 21 runs in two industrial manufacturing case studies. • Demonstrates feasibility for scenario exploration while highlighting challenges in output consistency and reliability.

title: Knowledge-guided multimodal LLM with mixture-of-experts for interpretable defect detection and fault diagnosis: An industrial AI copilot
abstract: The rapid evolution of smart manufacturing has led to an explosion of multimodal data generated from sensors, such as vibration signals, acoustic waves, and surface images. However, traditional learning models often focus on single-modal analysis and lack interpretability, limiting their generalization across different industrial tasks. To address these challenges, this study proposes industrial AI copilot QwIndustry, a multimodal large language model (LLM) designed for industrial tasks, including defect detection and fault diagnosis. The framework integrates a Knowledge-guided Mixture-of-Experts (K-MoE) architecture, which selects different expert neural networks based on the specific industrial task. The parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is adopted to fine-tune Qwen2.5VL, and Chain-of-Thought (COT) distillation to facilitate knowledge-driven multimodal reasoning, enabling the model to achieve reasoning capabilities at a low computational cost. Five diverse industrial datasets involving signal, image, and text modalities were employed to train and evaluate the model. Experimental results show that the proposed QwIndustry with thinking mode achieves superior accuracy over 98% on same-domain tasks and strong cross-domain transferability with accuracy around 95%, maintaining high recognition accuracy on unseen datasets without retraining. Moreover, the model provides human operators with accessible, interpretable reasoning results through natural-language interaction, eliminating the need for deep technical expertise. These results indicate that the Industrial AI Copilot provides an effective and scalable pathway toward knowledge-augmented, human-centric, and interpretable industrial intelligence.

title: An SFDPose network with credible evolution mechanism for digital twin systems in industrial applications
abstract: The rapid rise of Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things (IoT) has elevated digital twins from a novel concept to an indispensable tool for real-time monitoring, prediction, and optimization in complex systems. Yet, maintaining the accuracy and reliability of digital twins remains a formidable challenge. As physical entities evolve and operational environments shift, especially in data-driven and resource-constrained contexts, digital twins are prone to degradation, reducing their value and trustworthiness. To address these challenges, in this paper, we introduce a framework that integrates a Separated-Feature Dual-Branch Pose Network (SFDPoseNet) with a credible evolution mechanism. The architecture disentangles and extracts both long-term and short-term features of the twin system in parallel. Specifically, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks capture long-range temporal dependencies, while Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) extract multi-scale local patterns. We propose a lightweight residual Feedforward Neural Network (FFN) that integrates features from dual branches to achieve robust and expressive multivariate time-series forecasting. Complementing this hybrid model, an uncertainty-aware online evolution strategy ensures adaptability. Real-time prediction errors trigger dynamic model updates, while incremental learning with Fisher information–based regularization stabilizes the adaptation process and mitigates catastrophic forgetting. Extensive validation on a quadrotor UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) flight dataset confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art temporal prediction models in both forecasting accuracy and adaptability. Additional ablation studies highlight the distinct contributions of the dual-branch architecture and the evolution mechanism, underscoring the framework’s capability to sustain digital twin reliability under dynamic conditions.

title: Twist-pull as an execution skill primitive for robotic disassembly: Safety-aware skill augmentation under contact uncertainty
abstract: Structural variability and hidden contact interactions in robotic disassembly impede conventional task-specific control and learning paradigms. This paper formulates twist-pull (TP) as a fundamental execution skill primitive, a generic interaction pattern underpinning diverse disassembly operations, and proposes a safety-aware skill augmentation framework. Distinct from object-specific policy learning, this approach augments the primitive’s compliant baseline via reinforcement learning (RL) to accommodate unmodeled contact dynamics. To ensure safe exploration, the framework integrates a Safety Policy (SP) for velocity stabilisation and employs a structured observation-action architecture. By explicitly decoupling planar motion regulation from axial compliance modulation, this architectural constraint prevents unsafe force-motion coupling during policy optimisation. Experimental validation across structurally diverse components, spanner-type configurations, and real-world products demonstrates that augmenting the TP primitive significantly enhances execution robustness and generalisability, establishing a scalable foundation for contact-rich disassembly automation. • Twist-Pull is formulated as a generic execution skill primitive for contact-rich disassembly. • A safety-aware framework augments compliant baseline skills via Reinforcement Learning. • Structured network architecture decouples motion and compliance to prevent unsafe coupling. • A dedicated Safety Policy stabilizes velocity modulation during trial-and-error exploration. • The approach generalizes to spanner-mediated operations and diverse industrial products.

title: An LLM-enhanced knowledge service methodology for manufacturing process planning based on task- guided multi-layer knowledge graph
abstract: Manufacturing process planning is a progressive design process where designers use digital modeling information as a starting point to meticulously plan and optimize the product manufacturing workflow. This process involving repeated consideration of elements such as processing units, manufacturing operations and operation steps. Process planning is characterized as a hierarchical design process driven by stage-specific task objectives, in which decision constraints evolve progressively. The knowledge requirements for tasks at different stages not only influence the prioritization of knowledge focus but also impose differentiated demands on knowledge granularity, association patterns, and reasoning approaches. Thus, supporting multi-stage, multi-type decision-making simultaneously within a unified knowledge organization framework presents a critical and complex challenge. This study proposes a knowledge service model for process planning based on multi-layer knowledge graph. An iterative interaction model between knowledge evolution and process planning is proposed, in which four representative planning scenarios are explicitly characterized to reflect cross-stage reasoning requirements. Four process-planning-oriented retrieval strategies are defined, enabling differentiated retrieval mechanisms to accommodate heterogeneous task demands and planning objectives. A collaborative workflow integrating large language models (LLMs) and knowledge graphs is adopted to achieve unified semantic modeling and structured knowledge extraction of multi-source process knowledge. The proposed method was validated using civil aircraft bracket component manufacturing process planning tasks as verification cases.

title: Dynamic-static knowledge graph enhanced LLM reasoning for intelligent process planning in steel manufacturing
abstract: As a crucial step in steel manufacturing, process planning significantly improves production efficiency and product quality. With the development of knowledge graph (KG) technologies, significant progress has been made in using historical knowledge for intelligent process planning. However, existing KG-based methods mostly rely on static knowledge reuse, which fails to accommodate real-time fluctuations of smelting conditions in steel manufacturing. Moreover, the generation of process planning strategies remains heavily dependent on human expertise, making it time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic-static KG-enhanced Large Language Model (LLM)-based intelligent process planning method for steel manufacturing. Firstly, a static smelting process KG (SSPKG) is introduced to organize historical smelting knowledge using a convolutional block attention mechanism-enhanced partitioned fusion Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CBAM-PFKAN). Then, a dynamic smelting condition KG (DSCKG) is established to convert the real-time smelting conditions into structured knowledge triples based on predefined rules. Secondly, a plan-and-solve (PS) prompting strategy is designed to guide LLMs in decomposing complex process optimization queries, retrieving both static and dynamic knowledge from the KGs, and generating process schemes step-by-step. Finally, the proposed method is validated through an industry case study. Compared to baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves superior performance in process knowledge extraction, improving the accuracy of generated process strategies by 11.13% on DeepSeek and 8.63% on ChatGPT-3.5, respectively.

title: Long causal chain-of-thought for compound fault diagnosis: enhancing hypergraph-based Causal-LLM intervention reasoning
abstract: Equipment fault-investigation documents contain rich semantic information that implicitly describes causal states and failure mechanisms of key components. However, due to the high complexity of equipment faults and the dynamic evolution of causal chains after interventions, current LLMs struggle to model long-chain causal relations and multi-coupled composite-fault semantics. These limitations hinder accurate inference of intervention effects and constrain effective root-cause localization and solution decision-making. To address these challenges, we propose the long causal chain-of-thought (LC-CoT) method, which enhances hypergraph-based Causal-LLM intervention reasoning for compound fault diagnosis (CFD). First, a few-shot LC-CoT prompting strategy guides the LLM to analyze fault trees hierarchically and automatically construct a causal knowledge hypergraph (CKH). Second, a reinforcement learning strategy with causal-intervention feedback is employed to train the Causal-LLM for long-chain causal reasoning and dynamic intervention. Third, an LC-CoT reasoning algorithm integrates fine-grained CKH retrieval with intervention reasoning, enabling accurate diagnosis in compound fault scenarios. Finally, a CKH was constructed based on a bridge-crane case study, and 47,466 triplets were employed to train the Causal-LLM. Ablation and comparative experiments on CFD tasks further demonstrated the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed method in root-cause analysis, solution decision-making, and intervention reasoning.
keywords: Reinforcement learning with causal intervention feedback

title: Diffusion-guided hierarchical reinforcement learning with admittance control for multiple peg-in-hole robotic assembly
abstract: Robotic multiple peg-in-hole assembly faces challenges stemming from high-dimensional spatial coupling with complex constraints, difficulties in visual localization, force sensing and compliant control, and limited policy generalization. To address these issues, we develop a hierarchical strategy learning method that integrates diffusion-based deep reinforcement learning with admittance control. Specifically, to realize expert-guided insertion behaviors for assembly, the overall policy is decomposed into a high-level decision layer and a low-level execution layer. The high level employs a conditional diffusion policy to generate subgoals and updates them using an SAC value function, thereby accelerating learning and improving generalization. The low level adopts a TD3 continuous controller whose actions are fused online with admittance-based compliant control under physical constraints. During training, to reduce cross-layer optimization mismatch, an off-policy correction mechanism is introduced to mitigate instability due to optimization mismatch between layers and to rectify distributional bias. Comparative evaluations and experiments show that, relative to PPO and PPO+AC, the proposed method increases assembly success rate by 18.7% and 7.9%, respectively, while reducing the number of assembly steps by 130.7% and 38.0%. Compared with DDPG, it achieves success rate improvements of 32.5% and 15.8%, with step reductions of 261.5% and 54.9%. The method achieves smaller contact forces and fewer steps, with repeated trials attaining a 95% success rate; the maximum normal contact force along the Z axis is about 5 N and the maximum torque is about 0.2 N m, validating that the proposed hierarchical strategy yields superior skill learning and higher assembly success.

title: Reinforcement learning for energy-efficient multi-objective dynamic planning of hot rolling production
abstract: The energy-efficient multi-objective dynamic planning problem (EEMODPP) of hot rolling production is a pivotal production management task in steel enterprises. In particular, the dynamic nature and multiple conflicting objectives of the EEMODPP necessitate an intelligent planning approach that can rapidly respond to disruptions in the production environment while making effective trade-offs. To address this, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based predictive-reactive framework is proposed to efficiently generate an initial plan and reactive plans in response to five types of dynamic events, including urgent order insertion, order property modification, machine deterioration, downstream requirements, and periodical replanning. First, a novel mathematical model for the EEMODPP is established to minimize production cost, tardiness, energy consumption, and schedule instability simultaneously. Second, to efficiently solve each replanning problem, a multi-objective pointer network with knowledge transfer (MOPN-KT) is developed. Specifically, the EEMODPP is reformulated as a series of Markov decision processes after decomposition into scalarized subproblems, where DRL policies are parameterized as pointer networks to make sequential decisions by forming probability distributions over unplanned orders. Third, variable neighborhood search (VNS) is integrated into the training process of MOPN-KT to enhance policy learning, while an incremental reference vector activation-based knowledge transfer strategy is proposed to accelerate training. Ablation experiments validate the effectiveness of the VNS integration and the knowledge transfer strategy. Comparative tests against state-of-the-art multi-objective optimization methods on synthetic instances demonstrate the superiority of MOPN-KT in terms of solution quality and running time. Finally, a real-world case study from a steel company verifies its practical applicability.

title: Operational mode discovery and causal analysis for cascading failure detection and environmental monitoring: A case study in automatic assembly systems
abstract: Traditional predictive maintenance approaches in assembly systems often overlook the complex interplay between operational modes and their distinct failure propagation mechanisms. This study contributes to predictive maintenance within the Industry 5.0 paradigm by introducing an unsupervised operational-mode learning and causal forecasting framework designed to jointly enhance operational reliability and environmental sustainability. The proposed methodology integrates unsupervised operational-mode discovery, supervised classification for real-time mode identification, and mode-conditioned Granger causal analysis to uncover context-dependent causal dependencies among system variables, forming the causal foundation for mode-specific forecasting models. A three-station automatic assembly line with shared resources serves as the validation case study, using over 190 days of multi-sensor operational data. The mode-specific analysis reveals three fundamentally distinct causal topologies: a sustainability-driven mode, where carbon-footprint and power metrics act as dominant causal drivers; an operator-interaction-driven mode, where human–machine delays generate multi-path cascades across subsystems; and an emergency-propagation mode, where failures propagate bidirectionally between stations, forming tightly coupled cascading loops. By analyzing mode-specific causal structures, the proposed framework demonstrates improved interpretability of failure propagation mechanisms across operational contexts and provides a principled basis for developing mode-specific causal forecasting models. Moreover, the integration of environmental indicators into the causal layer enables a dual-objective analysis that links reliability degradation with sustainability impact. The findings highlight how mode-aware causal analysis can support context-adaptive and sustainability-oriented predictive maintenance, while positioning mode-specific multivariate regression forecasting as a natural extension of the proposed framework. • Introduces an operational mode discovery and causal analysis framework for Industry 5.0 assembly systems. • Integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to identify context-dependent failure propagation regimes. • Uses Granger causality to link sustainability indicators with reliability via mode-specific topologies. • Empirically validates the framework on assembly lines, proving stability over unstable global baselines. • Identifies dominant cascading failure pathways through spectral analysis and propagation intensity metrics.

title: A review of Generative Artificial Intelligence for additive manufacturing: Bridging design, process monitoring, and beyond
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) offers great design freedom, enabling the fabrication of geometrically complex, multi-material, multi-scale, and functionally optimized parts. However, it also introduces unique challenges regarding manufacturability constraints and complicated interdependencies among design, manufacturing process, and material properties. Recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) offer new opportunities to enhance AM workflow through data-driven approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive review of GenAI in AM, examining how advances in visual generative models and large language models, ranging from adversarial, variational, and diffusion-based architectures to foundation models like GPT, are reshaping design generation, process intelligence, and knowledge-driven manufacturing workflows. By integrating AM-specific insights into the generation process, VGMs enable generative design for AM, future build status prediction, process monitoring image enhancement, and data synthesis for downstream model training. Meanwhile, the powerful reasoning capabilities of LLMs enable knowledge acquisition, text-guided script synthesis for design and executable code generation, and adaptive process optimization. The review systematically assesses model architectures, applications, and performance across AM workflows, highlighting current challenges in data availability, constraint integration, three-dimensional (3D) generation, multi-source information fusion, and benchmarking. Future research directions toward context-aware, physics-informed, unified, and trustworthy GenAI frameworks are discussed to advance material design and enable smart, adaptive AM systems.

title: Interpretable data-driven framework with multi-scale residual correction and SHAP analysis for strip profile prediction in hot rolling steel industry
abstract: In hot strip rolling (HSR) production, strip profile quality is critical to product performance and subsequent processing. Compared with finite element and mechanistic models that depend on prior assumptions, machine learning (ML) can efficiently capture the complex nonlinear relationships between process parameters and profile, thereby offering significant advantages in predictive accuracy. However, most existing strip profile prediction approaches rely on single “black-box” ML models and are limited to mean value prediction, which fails to simultaneously capture the overall evolution of the strip full-length profile and its local fluctuations. This limitation primarily arises from the inherent residuals of single ML model predictions, which are often associated with long-term process drifts or short-term disturbances during rolling. Furthermore, the lack of transparent physical interpretability in “black-box” models restricts their trustworthy deployment in industrial practice. To address the above challenges, we propose a novel paradigm for high-precision and interpretable strip profile prediction, which integrates efficient profile feature extraction, light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM)-based multi-scale residual correction regression, and shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-driven post-hoc interpretability analysis, thereby achieving a balance among predictive accuracy, robustness, and transparency. This framework has been successfully deployed on a 2250 mm HSR production line. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed feature extraction method achieves superior reconstruction accuracy compared with both the sixth-order polynomial fitting method and the legendre polynomial fitting method. In industrial applications, the proposed framework demonstrated high prediction accuracy for C40, with more than 93% of the coils showing prediction errors within ±4 μm. Moreover, the SHAP-based feature contribution analysis revealed the key process variables governing strip profile formation, thereby ensuring both transparency and reliability of the proposed prediction paradigm.

title: Large Language Models for manufacturing
abstract: The rapid advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have the potential to transform the manufacturing industry by optimizing processes, enhancing efficiency, and enabling innovation at an unprecedented scale. This paper presents a comprehensive study of LLM integration into the manufacturing domain, highlighting their ability to automate and enhance key tasks across the product lifecycle—including product design, quality control, supply chain management, and talent development. We introduce a systematic taxonomy of LLM applications aligned with manufacturing stages, and evaluate the performance of state-of-the-art models (e.g., GPT-4V) in tasks such as document analysis, code generation, design automation, and multimodal reasoning. Our study further explores the use of LLMs in manufacturing education, robotics programming, and the industrial metaverse, supported by real-world case studies and visual frameworks. Key contributions of this work include: (1) a task-aligned framework that bridges LLM capabilities with domain-specific manufacturing challenges, (2) in-depth comparative evaluations with traditional approaches, and (3) a critical discussion of limitations, deployment challenges, and future research directions. By consolidating emerging use cases and practical insights, this paper serves as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners aiming to harness LLMs for next-generation intelligent manufacturing.

title: Reinforcement learning for autonomous production planning and control: A systematic literature review
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern manufacturing systems demands advanced decision-making approaches for production planning and control (PPC). Reinforcement learning (RL), as part of machine learning, has gained attention in recent years due to its ability to learn optimal policies for decision-making through trial-and-error interaction with a dynamic environment. This systematic literature review synthesizes 196 peer-reviewed publications from 2018 to 2024 on RL for PPC. Using an established RL framework, we analyze algorithm families, decision mechanisms, optimization objectives, evaluation practices, and industrial maturity. Results show a strong concentration on operational control, especially dispatching, with increasing adoption of policy-gradient methods and multi-agent formulations. Reward design remains dominated by time-based objectives such as makespan and tardiness, while cost, sustainability, and risk-oriented objectives are mainly treated as secondary terms. We identify a persistent structural gap between academic validation and industrial adoption. The majority of studies validate in synthetic simulations, only a small subset uses real industrial data, and very few connect trained policies to physical testbeds. No reviewed case study reports sustained closed-loop autonomous control in a live production system under continuous operation. We consolidate reported research gaps into an actionable agenda focused on environment fidelity, transfer governance, standardized evaluation, and safety and assurance mechanisms that enable scalable industrial deployment.

title: DOGREAT3D: Multimodal 3D reconstruction of complex mechanical parts with diffusion models and geometric refinement strategies
abstract: Reconstructing industrial mechanical parts from a single image is challenging when the output must be a CAD-compatible triangular mesh and usable in downstream CAD/CAE workflows after standard cleanup. We propose DOGREAT3D, a CAD-oriented mesh reconstruction pipeline that combines pose-conditioned multi-view diffusion with reliability-aware multimodal fusion and topology-preserving test-time refinement to enforce cross-view geometric consistency. Starting from one image (and an optional short industrial prompt), DOGREAT3D synthesizes posed views, derives geometry cues via cross-view depth alignment, and fuses RGB evidence with depth-derived normals (and optional text priors) through confidence-weighted cross-modal attention. It then initializes a watertight mesh using screened Poisson reconstruction and refines geometry and appearance with a four-stage, topology-preserving schedule that preserves sharp features and sensitive thin structures. On a wheel-hub benchmark of 1500 parts, DOGREAT3D reduces Chamfer Distance by 14.1% and improves F-score@1 mm from 0.453 to 0.526 over the strongest baseline under a unified evaluation protocol. On unseen part categories and on GSO, the geometric components transfer beyond the training distribution, improving F-score@τ from 0.647 to 0.667.

title: Spatio-temporal graph neural network based digital twin surrogate for throughput estimation in general assembly lines
abstract: Real-time performance analysis and optimization of complex, multi-station assembly lines are critical for maintaining a competitive advantage in modern manufacturing. While traditional methods such as discrete-event simulation or full-scale digital twins can provide high-fidelity analysis, they are often computationally prohibitive to support rapid decision-makings. Surrogate models offer a data-driven, computationally efficient alternative. However, accurately predicting system-level throughput requires capturing intricate spatio-temporal dependencies in a production line. This paper proposes a novel surrogate digital twin framework based on Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks (ST-GNNs) to address this. The assembly line is conceptualized as a graph to explicitly model spatial relationships, while its temporal evolution is captured using a recurrent neural network architecture like a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network. This study also investigates the impact of temporal data granularity by evaluating model performance on data aggregated at one-minute, ten-minute, and thirty-minute intervals, respectively. A comprehensive comparative study is conducted, evaluating the proposed ST-GNN against baseline models like Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and standard LSTMs. Results demonstrate that a Graph Attention Network (GAT) combined with a Bi-LSTM network and a temporal attention mechanism achieves superior performance. The proposed model achieves the highest prediction accuracy with an R² score of 0.80 using a 30-minute data aggregation step, highlighting the importance of both model architecture and appropriate data resolution for creating effective digital twin surrogates.

title: A novel temporal convolutional network-transformer framework with assembly data augmentation for accurate micro-milling energy prediction
abstract: Precision micro-milling is widely used in advanced manufacturing, but accurately predicting its power consumption is challenging due to the high cost and time required to collect data under industrial monitoring conditions. This limits data availability and reduces the prediction accuracy of traditional machine and deep learning models. This study addresses the data-constrained prediction problem by proposing an assembly data augmentation strategy combined with a temporal convolutional network-Transformer (TCN-Transformer) model for micro-milling power consumption prediction. The assembly data augmentation treats time-series generative adversarial networks (TGAN), amplitude adjusted Fourier transform (AAFT) surrogates and Gaussian noise injection (GNI) as complementary parallel branches: TGAN learns the nonlinear distribution of power signals, AAFT preserves key spectral characteristics, and GNI enhances local variability. Their outputs are then combined with optimized weights to enrich the temporal and frequency information contained in small-sample datasets. On top of the augmented data, the TCN-Transformer model first uses TCN layers to extract multi-scale local temporal patterns and then applies a Transformer encoder to capture global dependencies between power trajectories and machining parameters, while Bayesian optimization is adopted to tune key hyperparameters. Validation on three-axis micro-milling experiments shows that the optimal augmentation ratio (50% TGAN, 25% AAFT, 25% GNI) significantly improves prediction and that the proposed TCN-Transformer achieves an R² of 0.896, outperforming competing baselines. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates data collection constraints and provides a practical tool for non-invasive micro-milling energy prediction in precision machining.

title: Accelerating biopharmaceutical innovation: A review of machine learning across the manufacturing pipeline
abstract: Biologics represent a class of therapeutic agents produced via biotechnology, characterized by high specificity, precise targeting, rapid efficacy, and significant therapeutic outcomes. However, their development and production involve complex, multidimensional influencing factors and inherent stability challenges. Traditional trial-and-error methods and process screening approaches incur high costs and low efficiency. Machine learning, as a powerful data-driven artificial intelligence technology, efficiently uncovers hidden relationships among intricate process parameters and enables accurate prediction of critical quality attributes, thereby substantially reducing development costs. With the proliferation of computational pharmaceutics, Machine learning-assisted development is becoming a mainstream paradigm. This article first briefly reviews the fundamentals and classification of machine learning, spanning from basic concepts to mainstream supervised learning algorithms and their applications in biopharmaceuticals. It then delves into the standardized workflows underpinning machine learning implementation. Subsequently, based on representative literature from the past five years covering upstream to downstream processes and formulation in biopharmaceuticals, a comprehensive analysis of machine learning specific applications is presented. Finally, an in-depth discussion was conducted regarding the challenges of data availability, model quality, and the application of machine learning in biomanufacturing. A prospective overview of emerging technologies was also provided, highlighting the potential application trends of transfer learning, hybrid modeling, digital twins, and process analytical technologies, with a view to achieving the realization of Biopharmaceutical 4.0.

title: Multi-stage Bayesian optimization for throughput improvement in stochastic manufacturing systems
abstract: Improving throughput in manufacturing systems requires not only the accurate identification of bottleneck processes, but also a plan that determines the order in which to improve them and how to allocate limited resources. Although bottleneck detection has been extensively studied, determining – under resource constraints – the improvement sequence and the amount of resources (e.g., engineering hours for maintenance activities) to allocate to each bottleneck remains a challenging task. In practice, industry often adopts a simple greedy strategy that sequentially addresses the most severe bottleneck first. However, due to interdependencies among processes, prioritizing a single bottleneck can cause bottleneck shifting to other processes, thereby limiting system-level performance gains. In contrast, distributing modest improvements across multiple bottlenecks can sometimes be more effective. However, obtaining the optimal improvement sequence for such distributed enhancements is highly challenging, since the number of feasible plans grows exponentially as the system size increases, making it a complex combinatorial optimization problem, and furthermore, because the objective function and constraints are not given in an explicit mathematical form, it becomes a black-box optimization problem with a high-dimensional and nonlinear search space. This study proposes a Multi-Stage Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework that integrates bottleneck detection with resource-constrained optimization to address this highly complex black-box optimization problem and derive the most effective improvement sequence and resource allocation. Within the framework, we combine (1) Gaussian Process fitting with Noise Expected Improvement for robust candidate scoring in the presence of noise, (2) Sobol’-based active-set screening for dimension reduction, and (3) Knowledge Gradient per cost policy for adaptive stage-wise budget allocation to systematically evaluate trade-offs among multiple bottlenecks and maximize overall throughput. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional greedy and myopic strategies, enabling more efficient utilization of limited improvement resources.

title: MA-APKG: A multi-agent LLM-based method for construction aviation product assembly process knowledge graph
abstract: To address the characteristics of complex aviation assembly process knowledge, including diverse knowledge types, complex hierarchical structures, strong semantic correlations, and continuous evolution, a top-down construction method for an assembly process knowledge graph (KG) is proposed. First, a multi-level assembly process ontology is developed to provide unified and standardized modeling of product information, assembly process knowledge, tools and equipment, historical cases, and their cross-level relationships, enabling structured knowledge representation and semantic consistency enforcement. Second, to cope with the semantic complexity of assembly process texts, a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent collaborative triple information extraction method is proposed. By integrating ontology constraints and a self-consistency chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism, the stability, accuracy, and interpretability of extraction results are significantly improved. Finally, a semantic embedding-based dynamic KG update strategy is adopted to maintain entity uniqueness and semantic consistency during continuous knowledge evolution. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in complex aviation assembly process scenarios.

title: Intelligent generation of 3D disassembly processes driven by multimodal large language models
abstract: 3D digital processes provide intuitive guidance for practical disassembly operations. However, current 3D process planning relies on manual intervention and suffers from low automation. With the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of large language models and their recent rapid application in 3D tasks, we propose a multimodal large language model-driven framework for the intelligent generation of 3D disassembly processes. Textual descriptions, multi-view images, and semi-structured data are extracted from the 3D virtual scene. Three methods employing different prompt templates are designed to guide the multimodal large language model in generating 3D processes across different formats. The generated processes are converted into the keyframe representation for evaluation. To enhance the generation performance, few-shot prompting and Chain-of-Thought reasoning are integrated. Six metrics are utilized to evaluate the quality and efficiency of generated processes. Finally, we collect typical mechanical product models from public assembly datasets and conduct generation experiments. Manually designed 3D disassembly processes serve as the ground-truth. Results show that the proposed framework generates reasonable 3D disassembly processes based on data from the 3D scene, validating its effectiveness and practical potential for intelligent process planning.

title: From artificial intelligence to augmented intelligence: A review of intelligent forward design of wire harnesses
abstract: Flexible wire harnesses serve as the "neural network" and "lifeline" of complex electromechanical systems such as aircraft, ships, and automobiles. Its design flaws directly affect manufacturing feasibility and operational safety, and may even lead to catastrophic failures. Owing to their hybrid rigid-flexible constraints, multidimensional deformations, intricate routing, cross-scale, and high-density integration, flexible harnesses exhibit extremely complex characteristics. These characteristics make the design of a digital mock-up for wire harnesses exceptionally challenging. Achieving effective modeling, simulation, analysis, and optimization of wire harnesses during the design phase—thereby enabling early verification of manufacturing compliance and identification of potential service risks—remains a critical challenge in forward design. This challenge has continuously driven the development of theoretical research mode and methodological framework in the field. However, compared with the well-established theories and mature methodologies of forward design of mechanical system, research on forward design of wire harnesses still has obvious shortcomings. It is therefore urgent to systematically sort out technologies and summarize the development trajectory to accelerate progress in this domain. Therefore, this paper surveys the evolution of forward design methodologies of flexible wire harnesses, with a particular focus on assembly configuration, from an intelligent design perspective. It clarifies research directions, development trends, and research opportunities for intelligent approaches in this field. First, this paper summarizes the forward design paradigm for wire harness characteristics, including multi-scale characteristics, the task framework, and the evolution—from manual, digitalization, artificial intelligence to augmented intelligence. It then reviews the current research status of intelligent forward design research for wire harnesses, emphasizing the application of artificial intelligence techniques such as computer vision, traditional machine learning, deep learning, and metaheuristic algorithms. Afterwards, according to the development requirements of new-generation intelligent manufacturing mode, the study further identifies human-machine collaborative augmented intelligence design—integrating emerging technologies such as mixed reality, generative artificial intelligence, and digital twin—as a key future direction. A prospective research framework for augmented intelligence in forward design of wire harnesses is proposed. On this basis, the paper analyzes key challenges and identifies critical research opportunities in four directions. The developmental trends, future framework, and research opportunities presented herein aim to provide systematic reference and forward-looking guidance for future studies on flexible wire harness, contributing to the ongoing advancement of forward design theory.

title: Planning and evaluation of hybrid manufacturing–remanufacturing systems
abstract: This research presents an approach to plan and evaluate dynamic factory value streams of hybrid manufacturing–remanufacturing systems (HMRS). By considering remanufacturing processes during resource and capacity planning, the proposed model enables the development of factory concepts that allow for better informed decisions regarding material flows as well as lower operational cost. The approach integrates a mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP) for station capacity and material flows planning, with a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) for the dynamic manufacturing–remanufacturing life cycle balancing. For the optimization of the MINLP, a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) is applied. The results of an application use case demonstrate the advantages of the early consideration of remanufacturing into factory planning. The proposed approach enhances manufacturing–remanufacturing systems and demonstrates the benefits of strategic HMRS optimized planning.
keywords: Capacity planning and production concept planning

title: Research on tool wear monitoring based on digital twin and contrastive learning
abstract: Tool wear monitoring system (TWMS)in the machining process can improve production efficiency. The existing TWMS has the characteristics of poor generalization ability of detection model, strong dependence on data, and difficulty in adapting to complex cutting conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes a tool wear monitoring digital twin system (TWM-DTS) using contrastive learning. Firstly, the user interaction and virtual-real linkage are realized through the digital twin system front end (DTS-FE), and the tool state can be perceived in real-time to obtain machining parameters and store them in the buffer. Secondly, this paper proposes a milling force calculation model accounting for tool wear. The digital twin system back end (DTS-BE) can calculate the milling force of different wear conditions in real time through the data of buffer. Finally, this paper proposes a contrastive learning model. By comparing the similarity between the measured milling force (MMF) and the calculated milling force (CMF), the tool wear monitoring under variable working conditions is completed, which provides a judgment basis for the tool change of the digital twin system (DTS) anti-control machine tool. The contrastive model is cross-validated, and the mathematical analysis of the verification results proves that the model has high accuracy and generalization ability. The actual effect of virtual and real combination, tool wear monitoring and system anti-control machine tool change is realized, which lays a foundation for the application of digital twin in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Active learning using hybrid surrogate tool life modeling for machining process optimization
abstract: This paper describes an active learning approach for part-to-part iterative machining process optimization using a hybrid surrogate tool life model. A probabilistic interpolating tool life model is developed by combining the empirical Taylor-type tool life equation and the model fit error. The probabilistic tool life model is then used to calculate the machining cost per part distribution. The optimal machining parameters are selected using an expected improvement in machining cost per part criterion. The method is validated numerically using experimental results; the results show a median convergence error of 2.2% after three tests over 400 simulations. The method is validated experimentally on two industrial applications for Ti-6Al-4V roughing resulting in a cost per part reduction greater than 23% after two tests. The described method is a robust solution for rapid convergence to optimal machining parameters in an industrial production environment.

title: Dual-stream adaptive graph convolutional network with enhanced skeleton representation for human-robot collaborative assembly intention recognition
abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA), which combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, has become a core paradigm for smart manufacturing in Industry 5.0. Dynamic action intention recognition is a key technology for seamless human-robot interaction. However, the complexity of industrial assembly scenarios makes it difficult for collaborative robots to accurately understand the operator's assembly action intentions. Most existing methods rely on graph convolutional networks with fixed skeletal topologies, lacking the capability to capture cross-joint dependencies tailored to different action samples. These approaches depend on a single type of human skeletal feature (e.g., joint coordinates) and fail to effectively integrate multi-level dynamic information (e.g., joint trajectory kinematics and bone-level geometric transformations), resulting in an incomplete semantic representation of human action intention. To address these issues, this paper proposes an HRCA action intention recognition method based on a Dual-stream Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (DS-AGCN) model. Firstly, a simplified human skeletal structure is designed by removing redundant joints irrelevant to assembly actions, making it more suitable for recognizing upper-body movements in HRCA scenarios. Secondly, to enhance the model's generalization capability against operators’ individual differences, six data augmentation strategies are introduced. Then, an adaptive adjacency matrix is incorporated into the proposed method to strengthen the learning of dynamic dependencies between human joints that are not naturally connected. Finally, a dual-stream feature fusion mechanism is proposed. By embedding a motion stream within the joint stream, the operator's assembly actions are characterized from two dimensions: raw joint coordinates and joint motion features, thereby improving the accuracy of HRCA intention recognition. In the experiment, a HRCA experimental platform for a cylinder gear reducer is designed and developed, and an HRCA action video dataset is constructed based on it. The proposed method is experimentally validated using this dataset. The experimental results, including the model's training convergence performance, the enhancement effect of data augmentation strategies and adaptive adjacency matrix, and visualizations of the learning process across different network layers, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with eight other state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method achieves the best performance on four evaluation metrics, with an Accuracy of 96.97%, Precision of 97.08%, Recall of 96.97%, and F1-score of 96.95%, demonstrating its superiority in the recognition accuracy for HRCA intention.

title: A new explainable artificial intelligence algorithm integrated with multi-agent system for joint decision-making of smart manufacturing systems
abstract: Smart manufacturing systems increasingly rely on integrated production, inspection, and maintenance decisions to achieve high economic performance while satisfying stringent quality and reliability constraints under nonstationary operating conditions. Fixed inspection thresholds and periodic maintenance schedules often fail to adapt to evolving equipment states, leading to infeasible operation and suboptimal profit. This paper proposes a new Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based Multi-Agent System (MAS) decision-making algorithm for quality-critical smart manufacturing systems, addressing production, inspection, and maintenance decisions within a unified framework. A data-driven wear proxy triggers condition-based maintenance, while XAI fidelity signals dynamically adjust both inspection thresholds and effective maintenance wear thresholds when explanation fidelity indicates unreliable predictions. Global feasibility with respect to false-positive and false-negative constraints is enforced through an augmented Lagrangian optimization that supports policy parameters over long horizons. Case studies using large-scale industrial data demonstrate that the proposed MAS-XAI policy significantly outperforms both periodic maintenance strategies and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy. Relative to DQN, MAS-XAI achieves a 14.28% profit increase. Compared with periodic maintenance, it reduces maintenance interventions by 55.2% while maintaining a strict false-negative rate of 0.82%. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves operational robustness and economic performance in smart manufacturing systems under dynamic conditions.
keywords: Integrated Production and Maintenance Decision Making

title: A novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model
abstract: In the autonomy problem of large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing orders, three steps are usually involved: allocating orders among enterprises, assigning parts to 3D printers, and arranging parts on the printer’s build platform. Among these steps, the layout of parts on a 3D printer serves as the underlying layer of the autonomy loop, providing the basis for obtaining feedback during part-equipment matching and enabling real-time adjustments. It also affects the allocation of orders among enterprises. Currently, artificial intelligence (AI) agents specifically designed for part layout remain underdeveloped, and practical engineering applications still rely heavily on manual operations. Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model (SPVLM), aiming to provide an effective AI agent solution for the autonomous parts layout stage. We propose an autonomy architecture for large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing. For the part layout problem in 3D printing, we propose a visual-text evidence enhancement method and construct a dataset of 10,000 scene samples. We further propose an improved generative reinforcement policy optimization (GRPO) technique to enhance the layout decision-making capability of SPVLMs. Finally, based on the SPVLM, we build an AI agent using a reasoning and acting (ReAct) architecture. The AI agent continually acquires part-layout experience through a memory-augmentation strategy and supports lightweight deployment. A representative subset of the dataset is made publicly available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RTYGFb2dvBAsXXD5v7OTXq07QpIXMcTA?usp=drive_link

title: Bridging 2D vision and 3D CAD: Integrating cross-modal deep learning and LLM-assisted semantic graph reasoning for spatial disassembly constraint modelling
abstract: To advance automation in the remanufacturing sector, this paper proposes a novel spatial disassembly constraint modelling method that integrates cross-modal deep learning with the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). A significant challenge in robotic disassembly is accurately identifying spatial constraints for used products, which often exhibit uncertain conditions and structural deviations from original designs. To address this, we introduce a cross-modal deep learning technique that unifies the detection mechanism for both captured images of used products and CAD models of original products, effectively resolving multimodal data fusion issues during model training. Furthermore, we leverage LLMs to construct and match semantic graphs based on the spatial positional relationships among components. This allows for the precise identification of the optimal matching CAD model and the correct numbering of detected components, thereby deriving specific spatial constraints for each component. The rigour and performance of this method are validated through a case study involving the removal of used bolster springs from railway wagon bogies on a robotic platform. The results demonstrate that the proposed method enables robots to accurately construct spatial disassembly constraints under complex and uncertain conditions, facilitating automated disassembly operations.

title: MET-Net: An equivalent-section mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning in bilayer tube springback prediction under data scarcity and incomplete physical mechanisms
abstract: Industry 4.0 requires transparent and reliable prediction of manufacturing outcomes, which is often constrained by scarce data and incomplete physical mechanisms. These constraints are particularly severe for bent bilayer metal tubes, whose springback prediction is essential for process planning. This work proposes MET-Net, a mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning that reuses abundant single-layer springback knowledge for data-scarce bilayer prediction. MET-Net maps bilayer cross-section parameters to an equivalent single-layer representation through a differentiable equivalent-section module, whose adaptation is restricted to two physically meaningful correction parameters. The model is trained in two stages: physics-based initialization and single-layer pretraining, followed by conservative bilayer fine-tuning with sparse physics-residual guardrails, and a lightweight affine calibrator. On a copper-aluminum rotary draw bending case, MET-Net achieves a median RMSE of 0.4835° using only 100 bilayer samples, approaching the accuracy of a single-layer baseline trained on ten times more data. A paired zero-shot environment-perturbation evaluation further indicates stable performance under environment-level perturbations. Beyond accuracy, MET-Net supports manufacturing transparency through a structurally interpretable mechanism pathway, DeepLIFT-based training monitoring, and post-hoc diagnosability analyses. These strategies identify validity regimes of the embedded equivalent-section theory and quantify where systematic correction is required. MET-Net therefore provides accurate bilayer springback prediction together with actionable mechanism insight for process planning under data scarcity and incomplete physics.

title: Proactive energy-carbon aware production scheduling in SMT lines: A novel graph meta-reinforcement learning approach
abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing requires Surface Mount Technology (SMT) lines to adopt energy-carbon aware production scheduling. Traditional paradigms treat machines as discrete states, failing to capture the continuous thermodynamic inertia of thermal equipment like reflow ovens. Coupled with dynamic electricity prices and fluctuating carbon factors, classical optimization and standard multi-agent reinforcement learning become inadequate. To address the deep coupling of discrete manufacturing logic and continuous thermodynamics, we reformulate the scheduling problem as a semi-Markov decision process and propose a novel graph meta-reinforcement learning architecture termed GMeta-MATD3. Specifically, graph neural networks are utilized to extract spatial–temporal topologies across production and microgrid networks. To navigate environmental non-stationarity, a meta-learning module is embedded within each agent to infer latent physical contexts and predict peer behaviors, enabling temporal energy arbitrage via deliberate “wait” actions. Additionally, an attention-based centralized critic dynamically decomposes joint values to resolve the multi-agent credit assignment problem. Extensive experiments on real SMT data coupled with IEEE distribution systems demonstrate significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. GMeta-MATD3 achieves the best Pareto front, yielding a 13.1h makespan, 1020.5 RMB energy cost, 810.2 kgCO2 emissions, a 1.5% tardiness rate, and zero grid violations. Crucially, its thermodynamic stepping mechanism reduces transition energy from 12.5 to 3.2 kWh/batch, and proactive peak avoidance cuts the load peak-to-valley difference by 34.5%, maintaining daily carbon intensity below 0.55 kgCO2/kWh. Scalability tests confirm that executing 500-batch schedules in under 500 ms.

title: Towards semi-supervised and unsupervised source verification of additively manufactured parts with sparse data
abstract: A common challenge for manufacturing supply chains is to determine whether parts were made correctly, using the intended machines and processes. This study presents a deep learning framework that can discover and verify the source of additively manufactured (AM) components from surface texture visible in part images, with minimal pre-training or supervision. We develop a machine learning (ML) architecture that integrates self-supervised feature extraction using a vision transformer masked autoencoder (ViT-MAE) with unsupervised Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering. A simple classification head guides feature extraction when labels are available. To evaluate the model performance, we procured 3744 AM parts from six contract manufacturers. These manufacturers produced the parts using a total of 11 Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printers. Part images were used to evaluate the model across various unsupervised and semi-supervised tasks for predicting manufacturing origin. With no part labels, the model achieves an F1 score of 0.595 identifying the specific printer that produced the part. With minimally labeled data, only 36 parts from a single build per printer, the F1 score exceeds 0.9, outperforming existing supervised models. The architecture identifies anomalous parts from unknown sources in complex recognition tasks, including Open Set Recognition (OSR) and Generalized Category Discovery (GCD). The model identifies other fine-grained manufacturing attributes including the printer model, material, specific build, and location of the part in the printer. The research presents an image-based deep learning method that could enable manufacturers to validate parts from suppliers in data-scarce environments.

title: Optimizing contact-guided search for robotic screw unfastening under position uncertainty in electronic waste dismantling
abstract: Automating the disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) is crucial for the circular economy and the recovery of strategic materials like Rare Earth Elements. However, autonomous fastener removal remains a significant bottleneck due to the high positional uncertainty and degradation inherent in End-of-Life (EoL) products. This research proposes a deterministic, geometry-adaptable framework that integrates deep learning-based vision for coarse localization with a Hybrid Force/Velocity Control (HFVC) architecture for robust unscrewing. Five search geometries, including the Circular Spiral, Square Spiral, Windmill Search, Raster Scan, and Spiral with Noise, are compared in simulation, identifying the first of these as the most optimal strategy for industrial applications. Unlike empirical methods, we mathematically derive the kinematic constraints — specifically the maximum allowable spiral pitch and the optimal rotational velocity windows — required to guarantee successful insertion without heuristic tuning. Experimental validation using an industrial manipulator demonstrates the framework’s scalability across four distinct drive profiles (Allen, Hexagonal, Torx, and Phillips) without any parameter readjustment. The system successfully absorbs initial positional errors of up to 3 mm, achieving an overall 99% success rate with cycle times ranging from 11 to 13 s/screw depending on the fastener type, proving highly competitive for high-throughput automated dismantling lines.

title: A graph isomorphism attention network and graph information embedded reinforcement learning-based dual-arm robot teleoperation and manipulation skill acquisition method
abstract: Many human working environments are arduous, and entirely replacing on-site workers with robots remains challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a teleoperation and manipulation skill learning framework for physical avatar robots. For teleoperation, a real-time, dual-arm motion retargeting method based on a graph isomorphism attention network (GIAN) and robust kalman filtering (RKF) has been developed. This method eliminates the need for manually labeled human-to-robot joint mappings. By representing human motion as graph-structured data and leveraging a learning approach with kinematic physical constraints, accurate retargeting is achieved. The RKF is adopted to suppresses noise and outliers for enhancing stability. For skill learning, the study introduces a graph information-embedded reinforcement learning (GIERL) method that integrates imitation and reinforcement learning. Graph features extracted by GIAN are incorporated into both the observation space and reward design, enabling efficient acquisition of dual-arm manipulation skills. Furthermore, a shared control strategy is designed by integrating GIERL with GIAN to augment manipulation, forming a synergistic closed loop between perception and decision-making. Experiments involving desktop organization, as well as dual-arm box lifting and transportation in both simulated and real environments, demonstrate the superior performance and practicality of the proposed framework.

title: Vision language model-enhanced embodied intelligence for AR-assisted HRC assembly: Multimodal cognition, task reasoning, and autonomous execution
abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly is pivotal to modern manufacturing, yet it suffers from critical bottlenecks that hinder its performance. The fusion of visual, textual, and operational multimodal information remains inefficient, and human-robot task partitioning is often ambiguous. This ambiguity arises from inadequate integration of domain knowledge with perceptual outputs, while manual assembly operations lack consistency and a notable disjunction exists between abstract task reasoning and embodied robotic execution. These issues collectively impede the intelligence and coordination of HRC assembly systems.
