To resolve these issues, this study proposes an end-to-end Vision-Language Model (VLM)-enhanced embodied intelligent framework for HRC assembly’s cognitive reasoning and autonomous execution. The framework adopts a closed-loop architecture with four cascaded core modules, synergistically supporting perception, knowledge reasoning, human-robot interaction, and autonomous execution. First, a VLM-driven multimodal cognition module innovatively fuses VLMs with BERT (textual semantic processing) and ResNet-50 (visual feature extraction), capturing fine-grained features of assembly personnel, parts and tools to generate structured perceptual representations via semantic triplets and state matrices. Second, a domain knowledge-driven reasoning module is developed, which constructs an assembly knowledge graph by extracting semantic triplets from corpora via VLMs and encodes domain experience into machine-readable form. It adopts Graph RAG for semantic alignment, conflict detection and structured retrieval, and leverages LLM-aided reasoning to decompose global tasks into robotic and manual subtasks with clear boundaries. Third, an AR-assisted assembly guidance module is proposed to enable seamless HRC interaction and precise manual operations through multi-dimensional guidance. It covers visual-textual prompts, 3D positioning overlays, real-time monitoring and remote consultation, translating reasoned manual subtasks into actionable guidelines. Finally, a VLM-driven robotic code generation module realizes autonomous execution by generating modular action functions, sequences and trajectory parameters based on reasoned task representations. Integrated with hardware components, it uses an embodied controller to convert abstract robotic subtasks into concrete physical operations. Comparative experiments with traditional models and LLMs confirm the proposed HRC assembly system’s superiority.

title: Adaptive parameter optimization for turbine blade manufacturing: A novel personalized federated learning framework
abstract: In high-precision machining processes such as turbine blade manufacturing, optimizing process parameters is crucial for improving production efficiency and precision. However, process parameter optimization in current industrial practice still suffers from two major drawbacks: the slow convergence speed of high-dimensional parameter optimization and the protection of manufacturing data privacy. To address these issues, this article proposes a Sophia Extended (SophiaX) optimization algorithm under the novel personalized federated learning (DecePFL) framework. Specifically, the SophiaX algorithm is proposed, which efficiently utilizes second-order information through adaptive estimates of diagonal Hessian, significantly accelerating the convergence of high-dimensional process parameter optimization for complex blades. Furthermore, the DecePFL framework is constructed, which achieves personalized federated learning (PFL) through parameter decoupling and performs decentralized federated aggregation, thereby ensuring the privacy protection of industrial data. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conduct experiments on three series of aviation turbine blades (Blade A, Blade B, and Blade C). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves optimization efficiency, reducing optimization iterations from 84 to 27 for Blade A, from 80 to 28 for Blade B, and from 90 to 38 for Blade C.

title: Chat with the manufacturing process: A knowledge-guided cross-modal large language model for machining condition predictive maintenance
abstract: Predictive maintenance for manufacturing processes has become critically urgent to enhance system reliability in modern manufacturing. This paper proposes a cross-modal large language model for conversational diagnosis of machining process, where an interactive decision-making system that integrates multi-source sensor data fusion and knowledge enhancement was constructed. Firstly, the study introduces a knowledge guided graph fusion method to address challenges in information integration. Secondly, a cross-modal image–text generation model is developed to achieve low-parameter alignment between time-series imaging features and language models, enabling the generation of interpretable diagnostic reports. Finally, to tackle knowledge fragmentation issues of general large language models in industrial scenarios, a domain knowledge graph is constructed, covering tool wear mechanisms and the impact of machining parameters. A parameter-efficient fine-tune strategy is employed to inject structured knowledge, mitigating knowledge hallucination issues inherent in general large models. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves an accuracy of 94.2% in tool remaining useful life prediction tasks, representing a 11% improvement over traditional deep learning models, while providing dynamic maintenance recommendations through natural language interaction. This research offers theoretical support for the development of human–machine collaborative machining systems in intelligent manufacturing, advancing online monitoring technologies toward interpretable and interactive paradigms.

title: Deep transfer learning with graph neural networks for the selection of manufacturing processes
abstract: The quality of process planning, linking product design and manufacturing, critically depends on selecting suitable manufacturing processes. In recent years, several deep learning approaches have been proposed for selecting manufacturing processes, frequently relying on synthetically created datasets. While such datasets allow models to capture general manufacturing patterns, they fail to reflect the complexity and variability of industrial 3D CAD models. As a result, the effectiveness of deep learning for predicting manufacturing processes is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality, annotated industrial data. To mitigate the effort for annotation of industrial data, this paper investigates deep transfer learning for the selection of manufacturing processes. Models are first pre-trained on a synthetically designed dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on smaller sets of real industrial data. The findings demonstrate that deep transfer learning enables improved performance in the selection of manufacturing processes.

title: CA-DLM: Causal-aware diffusion language model for interpretable industrial defective image generation
abstract: This research proposes a Causal-Aware Diffusion Language Model (CA-DLM) for interpretable generation of defective images to address the scarcity of defective samples in industrial settings. Firstly, a causal inference mechanism is integrated into DLM to establish a causal mapping among “natural language instructions, model causal variables, and defective image generation”. The counterfactual causal intervention strategy enables interpretable, fine-grained control over defect, texture, and background features during image generation. Secondly, a learnable Structural Causal Model (SCM) is constructed to disentangle semantic features into causal and non-causal variables, effectively separating useful semantic features from confounders during image generation. A causal loss function is also designed to enforce sparsity and acyclicity in the SCM, guiding the model toward a causally consistent structure. Finally, the causal intervention approach is designed to perform do-intervention on SCM to achieve interpretable defective image generation. The do-intervention activates relevant causal variables and suppresses non-causal variables according to the learned SCM, thereby enabling precise control over key defect attributes while preserving the consistency of texture and background. Comparative experiments across three public datasets show that CA-DLM enables interpretable, controllable generation of high-fidelity defective images, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Detection models trained on CA-DLM generated images achieve significant improvements in downstream defect detection tasks, with accuracy exceeding 95%. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing that high-fidelity defective images can be generated using only 30% of causal variables.

title: A compositional dual-hand action recognition method for LLM-driven assembly assistance
abstract: Effective assistance in manual assembly requires perceiving the operator’s actions in real time and advising the operator flexibly. Traditional action recognition methods classify a video clip into a single holistic label for one action stream, failing to resolve the parallel dual-hand actions or expose the fine-grained semantics for downstream assistance reasoning. Moreover, conventional assistance systems retrieve predefined content keyed to recognized steps and cannot respond to an operator’s situated needs, whereas large language models (LLMs) can respond flexibly but are too slow and hallucination-prone for the real-time, safety-critical path. This paper connects the two through a compositional action representation that expresses each hand’s action as a structured tuple of action verb , manipulated object , target object , and tool . A compositional dual-hand action recognition model, CoDuAR, is proposed to predict the action tuples of both hands in a single forward pass through a shared encoder and hand-specific compositional decoders. On the HA-ViD benchmark, CoDuAR outperforms state-of-the-art recognizers that require a separate model per hand, while using 23% fewer parameters and roughly doubling the dual-hand inference throughput of the strongest parameter-comparable baseline, VideoMAE V2. Built on the compositional representation, a dual-process assistance system, Assembly Copilot, is developed. A deterministic System 1, driven by CoDuAR, maps the predictions to a symbolic task state, tracking the task progression, recommending next tasks, and detecting operational errors in real time, while an LLM-powered agent, System 2, reasons over the symbolic state to answer the operator’s queries and generate post-session performance reviews, gaining flexibility without placing the language model on the latency-critical path. A case study on a gear-plate assembly validates the functionality of the integrated system. The results indicate that the compositional action representation can serve as an effective interface between real-time perception and language-based assembly assistance within the evaluated scenario.

title: A pose estimation method for aeroengine blade assembly based on geometric priors and reinforcement learning
abstract: To address the challenges encountered in the automated assembly of aeroengine blades, where non-conformal insertion, irregular boundary features, and insufficient pose alignment accuracy occur between the blade root and disk slot, this paper develops a force-vision-guided robotic assembly platform. Based on the 3D point cloud measured by structured light, a pose estimation method integrating geometric priors (GP) and reinforcement learning (RL) strategies is proposed. Firstly, the key tasks and coordinate transformations in the automated blade assembly process are systematically defined, the geometric constraint mechanisms during assembly are analyzed, and a mathematical chain linking point cloud input to robotic motion control is constructed for pose estimation. Subsequently, during the coarse registration stage, three types of geometric priors—planar constraint, coaxial constraint, and boundary contour constraint—are incorporated to improve the accuracy and robustness of initial pose alignment. In the fine registration stage, the pose refinement of point clouds is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and a hybrid sparse–dense reward mechanism is designed. The Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is then employed to efficiently optimize the registration policy. Finally, assembly validation experiments were performed on both dovetail and fir-tree blades using the CoppeliaSim simulation platform and a self-developed structured- light measurement system. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior performance over existing registration algorithms in pose estimation accuracy, alignment stability, and assembly feasibility. This study provides an effective and generalizable solution for the intelligent assembly of complex structural components.

title: Toward provably safe AI-driven perception and motion planning for robotic manufacturing: A review
abstract: Safety is a crucial requirement for robotic systems operating in manufacturing environments, where perception and motion errors lead to unsafe physical interactions and process failures. While recent advancements in embodied AI and learning-based robotic systems have significantly improved adaptability, their black-box nature and sensitivity to uncertainties make safety assurance challenging. In response to such challenges, this article provides a comprehensive review of safety-oriented robotic perception and motion planning, along with complementary safety layers such as Digital Twins (DTs) that support the validation and monitoring of AI-driven robotic systems in manufacturing. In particular, our review first establishes optimization- and feasibility-based problem formulations to analyze and categorize this broad topic from a unified perspective. Then, we discuss mathematical principles and methodologies for improving safety in robotic perception and motion planning, including their learning-based counterparts, as well as their synergies with existing safety layers in smart manufacturing. Finally, we identify key challenges and future research directions toward safer and more trustworthy AI-driven robotic manufacturing.

title: Multi-information guided adaptive transfer learning for multi-point deformation prediction of blades in CNC machining based on Auto-MultiDeF
abstract: As core components of aero-engines, the surface precision of blisks directly determines the aerodynamic performance and service reliability of the entire engine. During milling on CNC machine tools, workpiece deformation is primarily driven by mechanical factors and further perturbed by thermal effects, exhibiting strong nonlinearity and multi-factor coupling. Despite extensive research, existing prediction methods encounter significant bottlenecks: (1) multi-source monitoring signals are highly aliased and non-stationary, hindering the precise decoupling of physical features reflecting machining mechanisms; (2) limited sample sizes and sparse parameter distributions in target domains restrict the model's generalization capabilities; (3) the complex nonlinear mapping relationships inherent in machining processes are difficult to learn effectively. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a machining deformation prediction model (ATL-PAMDF) based on adaptive transfer learning integrated with physics-informed guidance and Auto-MultiDeF feature extraction. Firstly, the Auto-MultiDeF module is developed to accurately extract and fuse component features from multi-channel aliased signals via a multi-scale decomposition and multi-channel fusion mechanism. Secondly, a pre-training and fine-tuning transfer paradigm under joint multi-channel reconstruction is constructed to facilitate rapid model convergence under sparse sample conditions. Finally, a mechanical model with error compensation is embedded into the training process as a structural prior, guiding the network to learn deformation responses consistent with physical laws. Multi-point deformation prediction experiments on a self-collected blade dataset demonstrate that the proposed ATL-PAMDF model achieves superior prediction accuracy and stability compared to state-of-the-art methods (RMSE&MAE at least 35% and 24% lower, respectively). The results validate its exceptional performance in complex physical scenarios and under aliased, small-sample machining conditions. The proposed method also offers an extensible solution for deformation prediction of other workpieces in CNC machining.

title: SEIT-Agent: An experience memory enhanced inspection and testing agent for high-safety special equipment with risk-aware LLM evaluation
abstract: The inspection and testing of high-safety special equipment (HSSE) is crucial for ensuring its safe and stable operation. However, two core tasks still require substantial manual effort: damage mode analysis requires synthesizing dispersed damage-related knowledge, while equipment quality grading involves determining and applying standard-specified rules. Existing LLM-based research augmented with RAG mainly focuses on information retrieval and Q&A, lacking mechanisms to autonomously and deterministically execute context-dependent rules. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the special equipment inspection and testing agent (SEIT-Agent), an AI Agent framework that integrates an LLM-based planner, a specialized tool library, an experience memory pool and a domain knowledge base. The tool library encapsulates quality grading rules for reliable autonomous grading, while the knowledge base integrates damage mode information and is accessible to the LLM via a hybrid vector–keyword RAG approach. The experience memory pool stores successful task execution trajectories to enhance consistency and accuracy in repetitive quality grading tasks. Furthermore, we introduce an expert-guided risk-aware LLM evaluation strategy where domain experts define critical and supporting assessment points and an external large-scale LLM evaluates response quality under a critical-point gating mechanism. Experiments on real-world data from an HSSE enterprise demonstrate that SEIT-Agent outperforms baseline methods on two core tasks.

title: Rec-PdM: Decision-calibrated recursive multi-agent systems for uncertainty-aware prescriptive maintenance in smart manufacturing
abstract: Predictive maintenance creates industrial value only when uncertain health evidence leads to an appropriate intervention under asymmetric failure costs and operational constraints. We present Rec-PdM, a decision-calibrated recursive multi-agent system for uncertainty-aware prescriptive maintenance. Its six decision agents maintain specialized beliefs about asset condition, fault state, remaining useful life, economic risk, action selection, and verification; production-impact and human-prescription interfaces connect these beliefs to factory context and operator-facing decisions. RecursiveLink reconciles local beliefs with downstream decision consequences while preserving the provenance of each update. The method treats maintenance as a partially observable degradation process and calibrates prediction and uncertainty against decision regret, tail risk, feasibility, and communication overhead. Evaluation on six public datasets spans degradation prognosis, process failure, vibration-based diagnosis, and acoustic anomaly detection, with controlled decision studies of cost asymmetry, coordination, resource constraints, dependent faults, and operating drift. RecursiveLink achieves the best mean-cost rank among the evaluated coordination mechanisms, while calibrated Rec-PdM ranks in the top two in 98.3% of the evaluated cost regimes without an unexpected failure. Under shared fleet constraints, the coordinator remains in the top two by mean cost in 88.8% of 240 scenarios; prequential recursive guarding reduces unserved failures from 70 to 5 under drift. These results show that decision cost, tail risk, and traceable coordination complement predictive accuracy when maintenance evidence must be converted into action.

title: A production continuity-guided domain-generalized topological transformer for production line real-time health assessment
abstract: Conventional fault diagnosis methods primarily focus on improving the recognition accuracy of individual equipment while overlooking differential risks that various faults pose to production line continuity. This accuracy‑oriented paradigm tends to significantly increase unplanned downtime when equipment importance is unevenly distributed, especially in the presence of bottleneck processes. To address this, this paper proposes a production continuity-guided production line‑level health assessment method named unplanned downtime minimization-driven domain-generalized topological transformer (UDMDGTT). From the novel perspective of production continuity, the proposed method quantifies equipment importance and shutdown risks in multi‑process workflows based on Birnbaum importance. A process‑dependent unplanned shutdown risk matrix (USRM) is constructed as a core tool for assessing production continuity, and the downtime cost caused by diagnosis decisions is integrated into the model training process. The USRM is used to construct the production line shutdown risk loss within the UDMDGTT framework, enabling the model to strategically avoid high‑cost misclassifications on critical equipment. To simultaneously pursue accuracy improvement and downtime minimization, a multi‑task loss function with a two‑stage training strategy is designed, and a time‑varying equipment importance mechanism that adapts to process reconfiguration without retraining is introduced to enhance cross‑process generalizability. Experiments on a manufacturing system comprising one lathe and two milling machines demonstrate that UDMDGTT reduces production line downtime while maintaining competitive cross‑domain recognition accuracy. Compared with the ablation model without unplanned downtime minimization, UDMDGTT reduces downtime by 16.88%, 47.08%, and 26.74% on the three machines, respectively, with only minor decreases (1.33%, 0.56%, and 0.72%) in recognition accuracy.

title: ViSTR-GP: Online cyberattack detection via Vision-to-State Tensor Regression and Gaussian Processes in automated robotic operations
abstract: Industrial robotic systems are central to automating smart manufacturing operations. Connected and automated factories face growing cybersecurity risks that can potentially cause interruptions and damages to physical operations. Among these attacks, data-integrity attacks often involve sophisticated exploitation of vulnerabilities that enable an attacker to access and manipulate the operational data and are hence difficult to detect with only existing intrusion detection or model-based detection. This paper addresses the challenges in utilizing existing side-channels to detect data-integrity attacks in robotic manufacturing processes by developing an online detection framework, ViSTR-GP, that cross-checks encoder-reported measurements against a vision-based estimate from an overhead camera outside the controller's authority. In this framework, a one-time interactive segmentation initializes SAM-Track to generate per-frame masks. A low-rank tensor-regression surrogate maps each mask to measurements, while a matrix-variate Gaussian process models nominal residuals, capturing temporal structure and cross-joint correlations. A frame-wise test statistic derived from the predictive distribution provides an online detector with interpretable thresholds. We validate the framework on a real-world robotic testbed with synchronized video frame and encoder data, collecting multiple nominal cycles and constructing replay attack scenarios with graded end-effector deviations. Results on the testbed indicate that the proposed framework recovers joint angles accurately and detects data-integrity attacks earlier with more frequent alarms than all baselines. These improvements are most evident in the most subtle attacks. These results show that plants can detect data-integrity attacks by adding an independent physical channel, bypassing the controller's authority, without needing complex instrumentation.

title: Temporal task graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for efficient human-robot collaborative assembly planning
abstract: Human–robot collaboration (HRC) has emerged as a promising assembly paradigm that exploits the complementary capabilities of humans and robots to achieve efficient and flexible task execution. However, existing assembly planning methods still have limited capability in representing dynamic task evolution and often suffer from inefficient policy learning, which restricts their applicability to complex HRC assembly scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a temporal task graph modeling and multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for HRC assembly sequence planning. First, a dynamic node graph is constructed from assembly-task relationships to represent task precedence, execution states, and human–robot interaction dynamics. Multi-dimensional task evaluation indicators are further incorporated to establish a structured multi-agent learning environment. Based on this environment, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm enhanced by temporal graph network (TG-MAPPO) is developed, in which temporal graph representation and multi-agent policy optimization are jointly coupled to improve exploration efficiency and training stability in partially observable dynamic graph environments. To evaluate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method, two assembly cases with different task structures, including an electric gripper and an electric vehicle battery (EVB), are used for comparative validation. Furthermore, a physical HRC assembly workstation is established, and a real-world HRC assembly experiment for the electric gripper is conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can generate feasible and efficient HRC assembly sequences. Compared with conventional schemes, the proposed method improves collaborative assembly efficiency, reduces the overall operation time by 44%, and alleviates operator fatigue during task execution.

title: Geometry-aware deep reinforcement learning for real-time integrated scheduling and nesting in additive manufacturing
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a promising technology for small-volume and customized production. However, the diversity of parts, coupled with batch scheduling and geometric constraints on heterogeneous machines, poses significant challenges for production planning. Unlike most existing studies on AM scheduling that underestimate geometric features, this paper investigates a real-time integrated scheduling and nesting problem with dynamic batch processing and geometric feasibility to minimize the overall makespan across heterogeneous AM machines. We propose GeoPPO, a geometry-aware deep reinforcement learning approach based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The proposed approach employs dedicated state encoders and specialized decoders within an actor–critic architecture and potential-based reward shaping strategy to produce geometry-aware decisions for part selection, machine assignment, and batch formulation. Computational experiments are conducted on synthetic and real-world instances with representative AM machine configurations and industrial part geometries. The results show that GeoPPO achieves near-optimal makespan on small-scale instances with an average deviation of 5.3% from the best MILP solutions, while reducing computation time from 1200 s to 1-3 s. With increasing problem scale, GeoPPO outperforms MILP on medium-scale instances, whereas MILP becomes computationally intractable for large-scale problems. Across all instances, GeoPPO reduces makespan by 18.1% relative to the best heuristic, and achieves solution quality comparable to the metaheuristic baseline among GA, ALNS, and GWO, while requiring only about 1% of the computational time. Ablation studies and generalization experiments further demonstrate the efficiency and practical applicability of GeoPPO. This research provides an effective and practical solution paradigm for complex scheduling and nesting challenges in AM.

title: Simulation-based multi-objective decision support for Comprehensive Digital Twins of smart manufacturing systems
abstract: Decision support in Smart Manufacturing Systems (SMSs) often requires balancing conflicting objectives related to multiple system dimensions, such as maximizing the number of completed products while minimizing energy consumption and CO₂ emissions. Comprehensive Digital Twins (CDTs) integrate multiple system dimensions within one executable model to support multidimensional analysis and multi-objective decision-making. However, an automatically extracted, simulation-ready CDT is not inherently optimization-ready because controllable parameters, admissible ranges, optimization objectives, and decision-to-model mappings remain unspecified. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a semi-automated framework that prepares an automatically extracted CDT for simulation-based multi-objective optimization. Starting from multidimensional event logs, Multi-Flow Process Mining extracts dimension-specific Stochastic Petri Nets and integrates them into an executable Multidimensional Stochastic Petri Net represented in Multidimensional Petri Net Markup Language. An optimization-preparation layer combines model parameter information with expert-defined selections, bounds, and objectives, and maps decision vectors to executable model configurations evaluated through simulation. The framework is demonstrated using an illustrative manufacturing line for robotic assembly and welding with rework. The Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied as the primary Pareto-based optimizer, while equal-weight weighted-sum scalarization is evaluated as a comparative baseline. The NSGA-II Pareto-front approximation supports post-search scenario selection. In a 100-replication reference-model evaluation, the selected scenario reduced CO₂ emissions by 3.81%, while completed products and grid-energy consumption changed only marginally ( − 0.29 % and + 0.17 % , respectively). These results support the proof-of-concept feasibility of extending an automatically extracted multidimensional simulation model to multi-objective decision support.

title: ProcessLLM-R1: A hypergraph retrieval-augmented and reinforcement learning-driven assembly process planning for commercial aircraft
abstract: As a key stage in the intelligent manufacturing of commercial aircraft, process planning plays an important role in improving production efficiency and ensuring product quality. Traditional process planning relies heavily on manual review of scattered, frequently updated technical documents, which is not only time-consuming and labor-intensive but also prone to errors due to limited experience. With the development of large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based intelligent process planning methods have achieved significant progress. However, existing RAG-based process planning generation methods typically rely on static one-shot querying and passive filtering. As a result, LLMs lack the ability to autonomously assess knowledge sufficiency, which limits their effectiveness in handling fragmented process knowledge and complex interrelationships. To this end, this paper proposes ProcessLLM-R1, an intelligent method for commercial aircraft assembly process generation based on hypergraph retrieval and reinforcement learning. First, a process knowledge hypergraph is constructed to organize process knowledge, and hypergraph retrieval strategy is designed that can be autonomously invoked by LLM, thereby enhancing the models’ ability to dynamically acquire and organize process knowledge. Second, retrieval is modeled as a multi-round interaction between the agent and knowledge hypergraph, and GRPO is introduced to perform parameter-efficient fine-tuning of the agent, thereby improving its adaptability to process generation tasks. Finally, experimental results on the commercial aircraft machining and assembly process datasets show that ProcessLLM-R1 outperforms the evaluated LLM-based generation and retrieval-augmented baselines across the reported metrics. It is hoped that the research can provide valuable insights and support for the application of LLM-based solutions in the field of aircraft manufacturing.

title: A structured taxonomy of autonomous manufacturing systems: Capabilities, definitions, and enabling technologies
abstract: Smart manufacturing has introduced adaptive, data-driven systems to the shop floor and beyond. However, current deployments operate near their technological limits, lacking the contextual adaptability, resilience, and independent decision-making required to manage unplanned disruptions. Autonomous manufacturing systems have emerged as a promising solution to overcome these deficiencies. These systems fulfill industry’s growing need for proactive rather than reactive approaches, balancing efficiency, safety, and agility. However, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent definitions, inadequate classification frameworks, and unclear capability-technology mappings. Terms like adaptive, autonomous, intelligent, smart, and cognitive systems are used interchangeably, creating confusion that hinders broader development and adoption. Critically, manufacturing lacks domain-specific autonomy taxonomies comparable to automotive industry standards, preventing systematic capability specification and solution comparison. Existing taxonomies frequently conflate service robotics and military systems with manufacturing applications, which demand precision, repeatability, and interoperability. This paper presents a manufacturing-specific autonomy taxonomy developed through analysis of cross-domain industrial taxonomies and maturity frameworks. The taxonomy establishes a six-tier classification: Cyber-Physical, Intelligent, Smart (semi and fully mature tiers), Autonomous, and Cognitive manufacturing systems. Classic automated manufacturing systems and adaptive manufacturing systems are pre-autonomy baselines below the entry tier and are excluded from the six-tier count. Each tier is defined by distinct capabilities, decision-making authority, learning mechanisms, enabling technologies, and human-machine collaboration requirements. First, this work provides standardized terminology and capability-technology mappings, functioning as an analytical tool rather than an absolute classification that divides the world into rigid classes. Second, it aims to serve as a structured, practical reference to guide practitioners and stakeholders in defining system objectives, identifying enabling technologies, and aligning operational requirements with appropriate autonomy levels. Ultimately, the proposed taxonomy establishes a common benchmark for system development and evaluation toward achieving autonomous and cognitive production.

title: A novel machining operation strategy prediction method based on self-supervised B-rep learning
abstract: Manufacturing operation strategy, as a crucial element in part manufacturing, directly impacts processing efficiency and manufacturing quality. Current machine learning-based manufacturing operation decision methods inevitably lose geometric and topological information when converting 3D CAD models into intermediate formats such as point clouds, voxels, or meshes, while also facing the challenge of insufficient training data. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative hybrid learning approach combining self-supervised pre-training with supervised fine-tuning that learns B-Rep representations from large-scale unlabeled CAD data to achieve manufacturing operation strategy prediction on small-sample datasets. The method consists of two key modules: first, a pre-training model based on an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder learns latent representations of CAD model face topological entities, and the decoder reconstructs the signed distance function of model faces; second, a supervised learning phase that utilizes pre-trained facial latent space representations to complete model segmentation tasks based on manufacturing strategies and modeling information using labeled data. Compared to traditional rule-based 3D shape representation sampling methods, directly using B-Rep data representation significantly improves accuracy; compared to existing supervised learning methods based on B-Rep input, the hybrid approach proposed in this study demonstrates superior performance on small-scale training sets.

title: Physics-grounded multi-agent architecture for traceable, risk-aware human–AI decision support in manufacturing
abstract: High-precision CNC machining of free-form aerospace components requires bounded compensations informed by inspection, simulation, and process knowledge. Off-the-shelf large language model (LLM) assistants can generate text, but they do not reliably execute risk-constrained multi-step numerical workflows or provide auditable provenance for high-stakes decisions. We present multi-agent knowledge analysis (MAKA), a decision-support architecture that separates intent routing, tools-only quantitative analysis, knowledge graph retrieval, and critic-based verification that enforces physical plausibility, safety bounds, and provenance completeness before recommendations are surfaced for human approval. MAKA is instantiated on a Ti-6Al-4V rotor blade machining testbed by fusing virtual-machining path-tracking error fields, cutting-force and deflection simulations, and scan-based 3D inspection deviation maps from 16 blades. The analysis decomposes deviation into an evidence-linked pathing component, a drift-based wear proxy capturing systematic evolution across parts, and a residual systematic compliance term. In a three-level tool-orchestration benchmark spanning single-step to three-or-more-step stateful sequences, MAKA increased the pass rate for correct tool selection, argument assignment, and dependency-consistent execution by a mean, median, and maximum of 22.9, 8.0, and 64.0 percentage points, respectively, across 15 model-level comparisons over the stronger of the ReAct-style and structured function-calling baselines with identical model and tool access. Digital twin what-if studies show MAKA can coordinate traceable compensation candidates that reduce predicted surface deviation from order 10−2 in to approximately ±10−3 in over most of the blade within the simulation environment, providing a pre-deployment verification signal for risk-aware human decision-making.

title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning using a world model for multi-objective optimization of micro-milling
abstract: Existing micro-milling optimization methods often rely on fixed objective weights or direct parameter control, limiting their ability to handle state-dependent trade-offs among surface quality, energy consumption, and machining time. This study proposes a preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic framework with a learned world model for sequential parameter optimization. Unlike direct-parameter reinforcement learning, the proposed method separates objective-level preference learning from feasible command generation. A high-level Dirichlet policy selects an interpretable preference vector over surface quality, energy, and time, while a constrained inverse control module maps it to spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut within prescribed bounds and rate limits. A multimodal temporal convolutional gated recurrent unit (MTC-GRU) world model trained on 900 physical Ti-6Al-4V micro-milling trials serves as the rollout environment for policy learning. Controller performance is evaluated through closed-loop rollouts within the frozen learned environment, while three predetermined variable-parameter trajectories, each physically replayed nine times, are used to assess recursive world-model fidelity under low, medium, and high transition intensities. Within the learned environment, preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic (PC-HAC) improves surface quality, energy use, and machining time under the stationary objective, and achieves larger gains in the cumulative energy-budget task. At κ = 0.80, PC-HAC reduced the budget-penalized score by 53.9% relative to the greedy controller. The recursive physical replay evaluation yields overall R2 values of 0.810 for surface roughness and 0.975 for energy, with prediction error increasing as transition magnitude increases. These findings support the proposed preference-space control strategy within the investigated micro-milling setting and provide a foundation for future physical closed-loop validation.

title: Physics-data fusion multi-modal deep learning for spindle current prediction in digital twin-driven machining state perception
abstract: Accurate perception of machining states is essential for intelligent Computer Numerical Control (CNC) systems, yet modeling key process variables remains challenging due to the nonlinear and multi-modal nature of cutting processes. Empirical models lack adaptability, while purely data-driven methods often neglect physical constraints. Direct measurement of cutting force is challenging in practice, as complex workpiece geometries, limited ranges of detection instruments, and high deployment costs make large-scale force data acquisition difficult. Therefore, spindle current is adopted as a more practical and accessible variable for state perception. In consideration of this problem, this study proposes a physics–data fusion multi-modal deep learning framework for spindle current prediction in a Digital Twin (DT)-driven environment. The framework integrates multi-modal inputs, including acceleration signals, STEP-NC semantic metadata, and cutter-workpiece engagement (CWE) geometric descriptors derived from the 3D engagement volume, into a unified representation that is processed by a data-driven branch for feature extraction. The architecture features a Sequence Head for residual regression and an attention-pooled Point Head for next-step prediction. Spindle dynamics constrain sequence outputs through a physics-informed module. Conditioned on process embeddings, a multi-objective loss adaptively balances dual heads and physical heuristics. The framework, deployed in a DT environment, supports synchronized multi-source data acquisition and real-time prediction. Experimental validation on a dedicated DT platform confirms framework feasibility, consistently maintaining R2>0.95 and superior error metrics across diverse machining regimes.

title: Bridging cognition, reasoning and action for polymorphic embodied agents towards human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly with vision-language model and digital twin
abstract: With the advent of Industry 5.0, human-robot collaborative assembly has become a core production paradigm that combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic operational efficiency. Single-robot systems cannot meet the diverse requirements of complex assembly tasks. Therefore, collaboration between human operators and heterogeneous multi-robot teams is required for flexible and efficient manufacturing. However, current collaborative systems are limited by fragmented perception-reasoning-execution pipelines. Poor generalization of general-purpose models in industrial environments is also observed. Additionally, integrated safety mechanisms for dynamic shared workspaces remain insufficient. These challenges indicate the need for embodied intelligence, through which agents can perceive, reason, and act seamlessly in physical environments. To address these issues, a vision-language model (VLM)-enabled, digital twin-assisted polymorphic embodied agent framework was proposed in this paper. A complete closed loop of embodied cognition, embodied reasoning, and embodied execution was established for human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly. In the embodied cognition layer, a domain-specific VLM was developed to achieve robust real-time perception of human behaviors, assembly components, and environmental states, with integrated depth information for accurate spatial localization and collision detection. In the embodied reasoning layer, a digital twin system with bidirectional virtual-to-real mapping enables virtual pre-simulation and optimal task scheduling that effectively leverages the complementary strengths of human and robots. In the embodied execution layer, the model directly generates executable control code for heterogeneous robots, which is pre-verified in the digital twin environment before physical deployment. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional visual algorithms and mainstream general-purpose vision-language models on all evaluation benchmarks. The system achieves three tiered latency indicators for decoupled functional modules. It delivers ultra-low single-frame perception delay below 150 ms for environmental safety sensing, and attains outstanding reasoning accuracy paired with an online task reasoning latency of 0.75 s to support real-time human-robot closed-loop interaction. The 4.8 s full assembly code generation delay only takes effect during offline pre-generation before task startup. This offline process is isolated from the online control loop and imposes no negative impact on the system’s real-time dynamic response and obstacle avoidance capacity. Continuous robotic operation was ensured. Human comfort and safety were maintained through differentiated task allocation. This paper provides a practical and effective solution for intelligent and safe collaborative assembly. It also offers important implications for the development of next-generation intelligent manufacturing systems.

title: Intelligent assembly support systems for human-centric manufacturing: A survey
abstract: This survey provides a structured analysis of intelligent assembly support systems, examining how these systems perceive tasks, reason about assembly processes, generate support actions, and interact with human operators in complex industrial environments. A systematic literature review of 184 publications from 2015 to 2026 was conducted, combining thematic analysis with bibliometric and temporal analyses to identify research trends, technological developments, and persistent challenges across perception, reasoning, interaction, and deployment. The analysis is structured around three perspectives: perception and task understanding under uncertain industrial conditions, adaptive support for heterogeneous workers, and emerging technologies with implications for industrial deployment. The review reveals that current systems remain predominantly focused on vision-based perception, action recognition, and predefined support strategies, with limited consideration of perception uncertainty arising from visual ambiguity and environmental changes, variations in human assembly behaviour, and diverse worker capabilities and support needs. By synthesising fragmented research streams across technical, human, and deployment perspectives, this survey identifies a fundamental transition from recognition-oriented support tools towards uncertainty-aware decision-support systems that enable adaptive human–AI collaboration. Key challenges include robust perception under environmental and visual variability, adaptive support for heterogeneous workers, trustworthy integration of emerging technologies, such as large language models and human-centric digital twins, and practical requirements for industrial deployment. This review establishes a broader perspective for evaluating intelligent assembly support systems, proposing that future progress should be assessed not only through technical performance but also through adaptability, trust calibration, human autonomy, and long-term operational viability. The findings provide a roadmap for Industry 5.0 assembly environments in which intelligent systems augment rather than replace human expertise.

title: Synthetic data generation in smart manufacturing applications: A systematic review and outlook
abstract: Data-driven methods, particularly those based on machine learning and artificial intelligence, are transforming decision-making in smart manufacturing. However, these methods typically require large volumes of high-quality labeled data for training, which are often difficult to obtain due to limited availability, class imbalance, privacy concerns, and the high costs and time demands of data collection. Synthetic data generation (SDG) has emerged as a promising approach to address these challenges. Over the past two decades, SDG techniques have evolved through diverse paths, including classical data augmentation, rule-based methods, simulation-based methods, and deep generative methods. Despite these advances, the adoption of SDG in manufacturing is still in its nascent stage, with applications mostly confined to proof-of-concept demonstrations and narrowly scoped use cases. Furthermore, a comprehensive, systematic literature review of SDG in manufacturing applications is lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic literature review of SDG for smart manufacturing applications, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Drawing on 201 identified publications spanning 2018 to early 2025, the review synthesizes the current state of the field and identifies key opportunities for future research. Viewed through the lens of the product lifecycle, the findings demonstrate how SDG can serve distinct functions at each stage of manufacturing, thereby revealing opportunities for advancing its integration into various smart manufacturing practices.

title: Towards spatial–temporal intelligence on the shop floor: A cyber–physical internet constrained approach for LLM-based explainable traceability
abstract: The effective operation of manufacturing systems fundamentally relies on the efficient flow and control of materials across the shop floor. However, existing approaches primarily focus on functional execution while neglecting the spatial–temporal context of production processes, resulting in limited traceability and weak interpretability. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces the concept of spatial–temporal intelligence (STI) into shop-floor manufacturing and proposes a unified implementation framework with corresponding enabling technologies. To support STI, a CPI-constrained standardized traceability representation, together with a handshake mechanism, is developed to achieve cyber–physical alignment of heterogeneous manufacturing data. On this basis, a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) is constructed to capture production knowledge, and a spatial–temporal context construction method is developed to integrate real-time localization data, event information, and process dependencies into a coherent representation. Building upon the KG and constructed context, a large language model (LLM)-driven reasoning framework is designed to generate structured, knowledge- and constraint-grounded explanations of operational deviations and their downstream impacts. Experiments conducted in a pilot-scale physical shop-floor testbed demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an explanation correctness of 0.96, exceeding the strongest baseline by 11.8 percentage points, while the cyber–physical alignment mechanism reliably distinguishes compliant, inconsistent, and authorized reconfigured executions. The proposed framework provides a unified foundation for integrating spatial–temporal perception and intelligent reasoning, advancing the development of next-generation smart manufacturing systems.

title: Large language models for intelligent job shop scheduling systems: A survey of problem modeling, decision-making, and dynamic rescheduling
abstract: Job shop scheduling is a core execution stage decision interface that connects production requirements with shop-floor execution in intelligent manufacturing systems. Existing studies have mainly improved schedule quality for well-defined scheduling tasks, focusing on efficient and feasible operation plans. However, real manufacturing systems require an end-to-end scheduling process that spans requirement understanding, task modeling, algorithm adaptation, and execution feedback, which still lacks systematic support. Large language models (LLMs), with strengths in natural language understanding, contextual reasoning, and interactive feedback, offer a technical path for strengthening key stages of this process. In response to this trend, this survey reviews recent progress in applying LLMs to job shop scheduling and builds a workflow-oriented analytical framework. It analyzes the technical basis and capability boundaries of LLMs in scheduling systems, discusses their role in transforming unstructured shop-floor requirements into entity relations, constraints, and objective expressions, and clarifies how they enhance scheduling reasoning through candidate schedule generation and assistance to existing optimization algorithms. The survey further examines how LLMs extend from offline scheduling support to dynamic execution, where multi-agent collaboration improves the response of scheduling systems to shop-floor disturbances. The review shows that LLMs connect key stages of the scheduling process, enabling intelligent manufacturing systems to better understand unstructured requirements, explain scheduling results, and support human-machine collaborative decisions. However, current research still faces limitations in output reliability, traceable explanation, real-time deployment, cross-scenario generalization, and industrial data security. Future research should further explore domain knowledge enhancement, human-centered scheduling, multi-agent systems, and sustainable manufacturing, enabling LLMs to become trustworthy, controllable, and deployable scheduling components for intelligent manufacturing systems.
